# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Son of David — The Messianic King

---

**17:1** O LORD, thou art our king forever and ever;
for in thee, O God, is our soul glorified.

**17:2** How long is the time of a man's life upon the earth?
as is his time, so also is his hope upon him.

**17:3** But we hope in God our savior;
for the might of our God is forever with mercy,
and the kingdom of our God is forever over the nations, in judgment.

**17:4** Thou, O LORD, didst choose David to be king over Israel,
and thou didst swear to him about his seed forever:
that his kingdom should not fail before thee.

**17:5** But for our sins, sinners rose up against us;
they assaulted us and thrust us out;
those to whom thou hadst made no promise,
they plundered with violence and did not glorify thy honorable name.

**17:6** With pomp they set up a kingdom because of their arrogance;
they despoiled the throne of David in tumultuous pride.

**17:7** But thou, O God, didst cast them down and remove their seed from the earth,
for there arose against them a man alien to our race.

**17:8** Thou didst recompense them, O God, according to their sins;
it happened to them according to their deeds.

**17:9** God showed them no mercy;
he searched out their seed and let not one of them go free.

**17:10** Faithful is the LORD in all his judgments
which he does upon the earth.

**17:11** The lawless one laid waste our land,
so that there was none among them who practiced mercy and truth.

**17:12** They departed from us to a place of desolation;
they came not near to our territory.

**17:13** The enemy acted arrogantly,
and his heart was alien to our God.

**17:14** And all things were such as he was doing in Jerusalem,
just as the nations were doing in the cities of their strength.

**17:15** And the sons of the covenant, living among the mixed multitude of nations,
there was none of them who showed mercy or truth in Jerusalem.

**17:16** Those who loved the assemblies of the devout fled from them;
like sparrows they flew away from their nest.

**17:17** They wandered in the wilderness to save their souls from evil;
and in the eyes of those who were saved a precious thing was the soul living among them.

**17:18** In every land was their scattering by the lawless [one];
for the heaven withheld dew and rain from dropping on the earth.

**17:19** The springs of the deep were dried up,
which run from the deep places to the lofty mountains;
for there was none among them who did righteousness or justice.

**17:20** Their rulers were slain by the sword;
no one wept for them
because they were strangers.

**17:21** See, O LORD, and raise up for them their king,
the son of David, at the time thou knowest, O God,
to reign over Israel thy servant.

**17:22** And gird him with strength, that he may break in pieces the unrighteous rulers,
that he may purge Jerusalem from nations that trample [her] down to destruction.

**17:23** Wisely, righteously, he shall thrust out sinners from the inheritance,
he shall destroy the pride of the sinner as a potter's vessel.

**17:24** With a rod of iron he shall break in pieces all their substance;
he shall destroy the lawless nations with the word of his mouth.

**17:25** At his rebuke nations shall flee before him;
he shall reprove sinners for the thoughts of their hearts.

**17:26** He shall gather together a holy people,
whom he shall lead in righteousness,
and he shall judge the tribes of the people that has been sanctified by the LORD his God.

**17:27** He shall not permit unrighteousness to sojourn among them;
no man who knows wickedness shall live with them.

**17:28** For he shall know them, that they are all sons of their God.
And he shall divide them according to their tribes upon the land,

**17:29** and neither sojourner nor alien shall live among them any more.
He shall judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Selah.

**17:30** And he shall have the peoples of the nations to serve him under his yoke;
and he shall glorify the LORD in a place to be seen of all the earth;

**17:31** and he shall purge Jerusalem and make it holy as it was in the days of old,

**17:32** that nations may come from the ends of the earth to see his glory,
bringing as gifts her sons who had fainted,

**17:33** and to see the glory of the LORD, with which God has glorified her.
And he himself will be a righteous king, taught by God, over them.

**17:34** And there will be no unrighteousness in his days in their midst,
for all shall be holy and their king shall be the LORD Messiah.

**17:35** For he will not put his trust in horse and rider and bow,
nor will he multiply for himself gold and silver for war,

**17:36** nor will he gather confidence from a multitude [of warriors] for the day of battle.
The LORD himself is his king, the hope of him who is mighty through [his] hope in God.

**17:37** He will be compassionate to all the nations who stand before him in fear.

**17:38** For he will smite the earth with the word of his mouth forever;
he will bless the people of the LORD with wisdom and gladness.

**17:39** And he himself will be pure from sin, so that he may rule a great people.
He will rebuke rulers and remove sinners by the might of his word.

**17:40** And he will not weaken in his days, relying upon his God;
for God has made him powerful in the holy spirit
and wise in the counsel of understanding,
with strength and righteousness.

**17:41** And the blessing of the LORD is with him in strength,
and his hope in the LORD will not waver.

**17:42** And who has power over him?
He is mighty in his works and strong in the fear of God;

**17:43** He is shepherding the flock of the LORD in faith and in righteousness;
and he lets none among them stumble in their pasture.

**17:44** He leads them all aright;
and there is no arrogance among them that any should be oppressed.

**17:45** This is the majesty of the king of Israel,
whom God knows, whom he raises up over the house of Israel to discipline it.

**17:46** His words are like the words of the holy ones in the midst of holy peoples.
Blessed are those who shall be born in those days,
to see the good things of Israel which God shall bring to pass
in the gathering of the tribes.
May God hasten his mercy upon Israel!
May he deliver us from the uncleanness of unholy enemies!
The LORD himself is our king forever and ever.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Psalm 17 is the most important messianic text in the Pseudepigrapha. 'Son of David' (v.21), 'rod of iron' (v.24), 'word of his mouth' (v.24), 'LORD Messiah' (v.34), 'Holy Spirit' (v.40) are all rendered literally. Hyphenated compounds preserve construct chains.*
